1|//! Host plumbing for utility builtins (`cat`, `grep`, `sed`, `ls`, …).
2|//!
3|//! These builtins are ports of standalone command-line utilities: synchronous
4|//! programs that read `argv`, talk to fd 0/1/2, resolve relative paths against
5|//! the current directory, and exit with a status. [`Host`] hands them exactly
6|//! that view of the shell they run inside — as a value, threaded explicitly —
7|//! so no process-global or thread-local I/O state is involved: output lands on
8|//! the command's (possibly redirected or piped) file descriptors and relative
9|//! paths resolve against the *shell's* working directory rather than the host
10|//! process's.
11|//!
12|//! A utility implements [`Utility`]: a `clap` argument model plus a synchronous
13|//! [`Utility::run`] body. [`util`] wraps that into a [`Registration`] which
14|//!
